name: atlas
tagline: Can AI teach you what AI just helped you build?
description: When Copilot writes the code, you get the result without the understanding. atlas closes that gap. It watches your GitHub activity, generates phone-readable lessons grounded in both your work and Microsoft Learn, and tracks what you've covered so it never repeats itself. A quiet librarian sitting between your build sessions and your understanding.
highlights: Phone-first PWA with offline reading
Lessons generated by a Foundry agent grounded in your repos
AI-managed taxonomy that grows from what you actually build
300–900 word reads with citations and 'what to learn next'

name: amberRepublic
tagline: What if a nation sim used real statistics?
description: Can real national statistics and AI make a governance simulation genuinely educational — and still fun? You run Latvia starting from actual 2025 data: 1.86M people, 20,000 emigrating annually, NATO border tensions, unfinished megaprojects. Every policy decision ripples through the economy in ways you won't see for three turns — exactly how the real thing works.
highlights: Starting conditions from Latvia's actual 2025 statistics
Second-order effects — emigration causes workforce shortage causes more emigration
AI-generated events for unique playthroughs
Every decision is a painful trade-off

name: agentFlow
tagline: Can we make multi-agent logic visible and debuggable?
description: A visual playground for understanding how nauroLabs agents collaborate. It maps agents, tool calls, and transitions into a live flow so complex orchestration is easier to inspect, explain, and improve.
highlights: Visual flow map of agent orchestration
Tracks agent handoffs and tool usage paths
Built to debug and explain complex agent behaviour
Focused experiment on making AI systems observable

name: portaBaltica
tagline: Can a public dashboard pay its own bills?
description: NauroLabs' first experiment in self-funding. A live economic intelligence dashboard for the Baltics — 30+ economic, trade, labour, energy, environmental, and maritime indicators across Latvia, Estonia, and Lithuania, all from free government APIs with an AI layer reading the trends in real time. The hypothesis: free raw data is a commodity, but the interpretation isn't. Free public dashboard, paid API and alerts. Goal: cover its own infrastructure cost and fund the next experiment.
highlights: 30+ live indicators across LV, EE, LT — economy, trade, labour, energy, property, environment
AI insights generated from live feeds, not canned summaries
Free dashboard, paid API and alerts — Moonshot v1 of the lab
All data from free public APIs: Eurostat, NordPool, ECB, Open-Meteo, data.gov.lv

name: tPlan
tagline: Can AI turn a training book into a real coach?
description: Can AI read a training methodology book and act as a coach — not a tracker, not a generator, an actual coach? Feed it a calisthenics manual, it parses the progression rules, builds your plan, tracks your reps, and advances you when the book says you're ready. Turns out it follows the rules more faithfully than most humans. Real training data in, real progression out — and any book becomes the methodology.
highlights: Book → program: AI parses methodology into structured plans
Auto-progression follows the book's own advancement rules
Multilingual — English, Russian, Latvian, Spanish
Phase 2 web app live; user-uploaded books planned for Phase 3

name: rosette
tagline: Where the hell do I put my sockets?
description: Upload a floor plan, get a standards-compliant electrical plan. This experiment tests whether AI can parse construction codes well enough to tell you exactly where sockets should go, how many you need per room, and which circuits need dedicated protection. Latvian, Lithuanian, and Estonian codes are live — the kind of specialised knowledge that normally costs a consultant's hourly rate.
highlights: AI analyzes floor plans to detect rooms and dimensions
Country-specific socket rules (LV, LT, EE)
SVG circuit and wiring diagrams
Possibly the world's most niche AI application

name: golazo
tagline: Can gamification build better young athletes?
description: Can gamification make young footballers actually track their own training and match data? XP, levels, achievements, skill radar charts, and a collectible-style player card — built on coaching methodology from 10 football development books. Log a session, earn XP, watch the radar chart grow. The theory: if the feedback loop is fun enough, the data takes care of itself.
highlights: 50 levels with football ranks from Rookie to Pro
25+ drills from Coerver, Horst Wein, Dan Abrahams, UEFA methodology
Collectible player card with spider chart skills radar
4 languages: Russian, Latvian, English, Spanish

name: art
tagline: Can a personal gallery be just a folder of HTML files?
description: An experiment in publishing without infrastructure. A folder of single-file HTML pages where each piece is its own little corner of the web — no CMS, no database, no build pipeline. The hypothesis: when AI handles the markup and CSS, the work matters more than the stack, and a non-developer can run their own site indefinitely.
highlights: Single-file HTML pages — readable source, no toolchain
Push to main, live in a minute on GitHub Pages
Sister project to playGround — same pattern, different audience
Built for people who paint and write, not people who deploy

name: playGround
tagline: Can kids build their own games with AI?
description: An experiment in lowering the floor for who gets to ship software. The starter shelf has four classic arcade games — Snake, Tetris, Breakout, Table Tennis — each built as a single self-contained HTML file so a kid can open the source, change it, and put it back online. The hypothesis: when AI handles the boring parts, the catalog grows with whatever kids actually want to make. Four games today. The rest is up to whoever shows up.
highlights: Workspace for young creators, not a finished games arcade
Four starter games — Snake, Tetris, Breakout, Table Tennis
Single-file source — readable, remixable, no toolchain
Catalog grows as kids ship their own ideas

name: era
tagline: ERP that configures itself (in theory)
description: An experiment: can an AI agent read a country's tax code and set up the entire accounting system without a consultant? You throw in invoices and payments — the agent researches the legislation, generates GL accounts, VAT rules, and posting templates. No chart-of-accounts wizard. No consultant. Latvian tax law is live; the architecture is jurisdictionally agnostic.
highlights: AI agent researches legislation and generates accounting rules
Zero settings — posting rules replace configuration
One country done, infinite ambition
Entra ID auth, Cosmos DB, full cloud-native

name: agentMode
tagline: Do we still need apps if a chat agent can do the job?
description: A Telegram-based personal assistant that lives on a tight Azure budget. It orders groceries by literally looking at websites with AI vision, tracks expenses, hunts cheap flights, and delivers morning briefings. The experiment: how much daily-app behaviour can be replaced by a single conversational agent — and how cheaply? 22 auto-discovered skills today, running for the price of two coffees a month.
highlights: 22 auto-discovered skills — from weather to grocery ordering
AI vision fallback: when automation breaks, the agent screenshots and navigates
Full infra-as-code, deploys with one script
Multilingual (EN, LV, RU), ~$5–10/month on Azure

name: turgo
tagline: Can AI agents buy and sell better than humans?
description: An experiment in automating the entire buy-sell lifecycle with AI agents. The idea: you say 'sell this' with a photo, and agents handle listing creation, pricing, negotiation, and market monitoring. Testing different purchase and sales strategies to see what actually works when agents do the haggling.
highlights: Photo → AI listing → pricing → negotiation → sold
7 operational agents: moderation, analytics, anti-fraud, and more
Testing buy/sell strategies with agent-vs-agent scenarios
Multilingual: 5 UI languages, 3 Baltic countries

name: dealScout
tagline: Can an agent tell a real bargain from noise?
description: Can an AI agent monitor menswear sales and surface only the deals worth acting on? dealScout scans for strong price-to-quality signals, filters routine discounts, and emails a concise buy recommendation when an offer clears the bar.
highlights: Monitors menswear offers for unusually strong value
Filters ordinary promotions before they reach the user
Sends a focused buy signal instead of a deal feed
Runs automatically on a scheduled workflow

name: foundryLab
tagline: When is a managed agent platform the right tool?
description: Can one learning lab reveal when a managed agent platform is worth the added machinery? foundryLab builds focused agents for retrieval, scheduling, evaluation, multi-agent work, and vision, then records the cost and engineering trade-offs.
highlights: Five experiments spanning retrieval, scheduling, evaluation, orchestration, and vision
Shared comparison notes turn each build into reusable evidence
One resource group keeps infrastructure and cost visible
Smaller models are the default; stronger models are reserved for evaluation gates

name: homeScout
tagline: Can property data produce a useful shortlist?
description: Can an agent combine fragmented property data into advice a home-buyer can act on? homeScout gathers and deduplicates listings, compares asking prices with registered sales, enriches each property with practical signals, and ranks a daily shortlist against explicit criteria.
highlights: Combines listings, developer inventory, auctions, and registered sales
Flags properties as over- or under-priced using nearby transactions
Applies hard filters before weighted scoring
Learns from shortlist feedback without exposing personal criteria

name: nauroBot
tagline: Can one tap govern an autonomous build loop?
description: Can lightweight human approval keep autonomous software work accountable without slowing it down? nauroBot turns idea proposals into approve-or-decline actions, starts an automated build after approval, and feeds decline reasons back into the next round of ideation.
highlights: Closes the loop from proposed idea to approved build
Uses issues as the shared message bus instead of a database
Captures decline reasons for better future proposals
Designed to extend to deployments, status checks, and plan triggers

name: payArc
tagline: Can agents simplify payment operations?
description: Can agent-assisted onboarding, routing, and fraud review make payment operations viable for a lean team? payArc is a research experiment mapping the architecture, controls, and risks before any transaction-processing code is built.
highlights: Tests faster merchant onboarding with agent-assisted verification
Explores per-transaction routing and retry decisions
Stages fraud controls from deterministic rules to learned models
Treats merchant abuse as a first-class operational risk

name: mindMe
tagline: Can a personal agent reduce daily friction?
description: Can a deliberately small personal agent make a private knowledge system useful every day? mindMe delivers a morning briefing, captures thoughts into an inbox, and answers simple status commands while keeping personal content out of logs and public surfaces.
highlights: Focused first release: briefing, capture, status, and help
Mirrors markdown knowledge into a private cloud workspace
Logs only operational metadata, never personal content
Uses managed identity and a strict monthly cost ceiling

name: autoRefine
tagline: Can software projects improve themselves?
description: Can an agent continuously evaluate a software project and safely turn gaps into tested changes? autoRefine reads the project's intent and code, researches alternatives, prioritizes improvements, and either opens a change or asks for a decision when confidence is low.
highlights: Runs discovery, research, evaluation, planning, testing, and change creation
Supports direct refinement and idea-filing modes
Escalates uncertain or risky changes for human review
Uses tiered models to keep recurring evaluations inexpensive

name: memex
tagline: Can one link become durable knowledge?
description: Can dropping a link into chat reliably produce useful, cross-linked knowledge instead of another unread bookmark? memex fetches supported sources, extracts durable concepts and decisions, writes structured markdown pages, and opens a reviewable change in the correct vault.
highlights: Routes one ingestion engine across three separately governed vaults
Handles articles, transcripts, discussions, podcasts, and documents
Produces cross-linked markdown through a reviewable change
Keeps raw content private with lifecycle-managed storage

name: glassBox
tagline: Can a useful AI app ship without embedded AI?
description: Can a thin interface let a human and an external agent cooperate without embedding a model in the product? glassBox exposes semantic state and safe actions to the user's own agent, while approvals, an action log, and rollback keep the human in control.
highlights: Ships no embedded model or AI SDK
Uses semantic HTML and stable state for reliable agent operation
Requires approval for consequential actions
Provides an action log, live co-presence, and one-click rollback

name: courier
tagline: Can one tiny service handle every lab email?
description: Can a shared notification service remove repeated email plumbing without becoming an open relay? courier accepts server-to-server messages from lab projects and sends them through one managed email resource with identity-based authentication and a recipient allowlist.
highlights: Provides one send endpoint for every lab project
Supports formatted messages, text fallback, copy, and blind copy
Rejects recipients outside a configured allowlist
Uses managed identity instead of connection strings

name: folio
tagline: Can AI explain a portfolio without controlling it?
description: Can a local-first portfolio tool add useful AI explanation without surrendering financial data or trading authority? folio unifies portfolio views, checks decisions against a written policy, and drafts rebalancing suggestions for human approval while keeping real figures on-device.
highlights: Extends a deterministic portfolio engine instead of rebuilding one
Explains and checks decisions but never executes trades
Keeps holdings, balances, and transaction history off the network
Sends only figure-free structure to optional cloud models

name: prime
tagline: Can a weekly brief make health trends actionable?
description: Can a personal health coach turn private trend data into one or two realistic next steps each week? prime analyzes locally prepared health and habit signals, flags meaningful drift, and produces a concise coaching brief without exposing raw medical records.
highlights: Processes large health exports as a stream
Tracks short- and medium-term direction instead of isolated readings
Falls back to deterministic coaching when no model is configured
Keeps raw medical data outside the repository and agent context

name: kiosk
tagline: Can an agent run a real local business?
description: Can agent-runnability be the first filter when choosing a real local business, rather than a later optimization? kiosk captures ideas, decomposes their operating loops, scores build-versus-acquire candidates on one rubric, and advances only the businesses an agent could run end to end.
highlights: Evaluates new ventures and acquisition candidates with one rubric
Weights agent-runnability above conventional attractiveness
Breaks each business into seven operating stages
Moves candidates through ideation, evaluation, planning, and operation
